beats.text: Every team has a hundred diagrams that should look the same. Fix one by hand, and Open Apprentice fixes the rest, and proves every edit.
Teach by showing. Powered by NVIDIA Nemotron, running on Nebius Token Factory.

Under the hood, every file is drawn by the real draw dot io viewer, in a locked, offline browser. Nemotron writes candidate rules in a tiny, exact rule language, and a sandboxed interpreter runs them. Nothing the model writes is ever executed as code.
Start with real draw dot io files. The apprentice measures every box the engine actually draws, matches each note to its box, and you check its guess.
Then show it once. I drag each note under its box, left aligned. Every move is redrawn by the real draw dot io engine.

Now Nemotron, live on Nebius, proposes programs that could explain my example, and each one is replayed against what I did. Several fit. Instead of guessing, a bounded search draws a test diagram where those programs disagree.
beats.onScreen: Live · NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory
explain: Each is run on your example
A test diagram where they disagree

beats.text: And it asks me one question, with a picture of each answer. I pick the one I meant.
explain: Your pick removes the wrong rules

beats.text: It previews the rule on diagrams I never touched, and stores it as a versioned skill. Every step goes into an event log that can be replayed exactly.

Now the payoff. A hundred diagrams, one click. Each edit is a byte exact patch of just the note positions, and every file is re-parsed, re-rendered and measured, passing three independent checks before it is published.

beats.onScreen: Floor plans · org charts · roadmaps · networks
beats.text: And it is not just flowcharts. Floor plans, org charts, roadmaps and network maps are fixed by the same skill, because it learned how notes relate to their boxes, not what one picture looks like.
Before, and after. Nothing else in the file changes.
The same show, ask, and check loop also works on other layouts. Here, an earlier prototype places badges on UI cards, across two different graphics engines.
beats.onScreen: Earlier prototype · UI components · Konva and Fabric

beats.text: We tested it on a frozen benchmark, and we publish where it wins and where it does not. It refuses when your examples conflict, it asks when they are ambiguous, and it never silently breaks your files. Open Apprentice.
